messages:

Cc: Eric Hayes <eric.hayes@telcoco.net>, prodops@edgeops.acme.com

Subject: Private VPC: control/data choreography + diagram annotations

Hi team —

Attaching the initial sequence diagram for the Telcoco private VPC deployment (control plane <-> data plane choreography). I tried to flatten the interactions so we can validate the handshake and egress checkpoints before the network dry-run. Key asks:

- Please review the control-plane RPCs and confirm which ports we should open on the control-plane ingress (currently 7443, 15017, and a gRPC port 50051).
- Verify the mTLS bootstrapping flow in the diagram (steps 2-6) — especially around who performs cert signing: Redwood CA vs Telcoco's internal PKI.
- Confirm expectations for data-plane egress: where telemetry/proxy calls exit (Telcoco NAT vs Redwood egress relay).

Attachments: control-data-sequence-v1.drawio.png (contains swimlanes for CP/DP/Edge/Telemetry).

Notes: this is aimed at the staging cutover on 2026-09-20. If you can annotate directly in Drive or drop quick inline notes here, I’ll incorporate and reissue a v2.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Infra PM, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Eric Hayes <eric.hayes@telcoco.net>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: control/data choreography + diagram annotations

On Tue, 1 Sep 2026 at 09:12, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attaching the initial sequence diagram for the Telcoco private VPC deployment (control plane <-> data plane choreography).

Nice layout — a few inline things I flagged:

1) Auth/PKI: we should standardize on Telcoco-managed intermediate certs for node bootstrap (Redwood will accept the intermediate signed by Telcoco root). That avoids cross-account KMS access during rotation.

2) Ports: 50051 (gRPC) and 7443 are fine for CP RPC. For control-plane telemetry we should use a dedicated port (15017) with a global allow-list limited to Telcoco's collector IPs. Don’t open 15017 to 0.0.0.0/0.

3) Data-plane egress: Telcoco has expressed preference to keep egress inside their NAT for auditability. If we need fallback to Redwood egress relay, ensure it’s opt-in per tenant and logged.

4) Observability: add a light-weight HTTP healthcheck (/_internal/health) called by Telcoco edge every 30s; don't rely solely on CP heartbeats.

I attached a tiny markdown with runbook edits I recommend (annotated-runbook-changes.md).

- Kim
Director, Platform Security

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Eric Hayes <eric.hayes@telcoco.net>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 08:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: control/data choreography + diagram annotations

Thanks for the diagram, Jonas — I added a second artifact (I uploaded an annotated PNG to Drive) that calls out two operational choke points:

- Edge-Proxy stateful failover: highlight that the DP connection to the edge-proxy is sticky by session id; if the proxy flips, KV-cache continuity must be negotiated. Suggest adding an inter-proxy sync step in the diagram (after step 9).
- Control-plane rate-limits: the CP needs request limits for tenant upsert APIs during cutover to avoid control-plane saturation. I proposed a soft limit + token-bucket backoff in the notes.

Action items I’m taking:
- Add a small section in the staging runbook describing how to force failover and observe KV-resync.
- Validate that we can surface token-level cost metrics for Telcoco during the canary window.

If Telcoco can confirm whether they'd prefer opt-in Redwood egress during the test window, we'll mark the fallback path as enabled/disabled in the cutover checklist.

Cheers,
Marissa
Sr. Reliability Engineer

From: Eric Hayes <eric.hayes@telcoco.net>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 13:50 +0100
Subject: Re: Private VPC: control/data choreography + diagram annotations

Jonas / team — thanks for the diagram. A few constraints from our side (Telcoco infra):

* We must terminate TLS at our L4 edge for DPI and DLP scans, which means Redwood's CP certs need to be usable behind our TLS termination model. Can you confirm cert subject naming will remain predictable (CN/service-tenant) so our WAF rules can include them?
* For egress: we will default to keeping all outbound telemetry inside our NAT and ship a mirrored telemetry stream to Redwood's collector (pull model preferred).
* Regarding KV-cache continuity: our operator prefers a graceful handoff window (60s) — if Redwood needs faster, we need to test it explicitly.

We can sign the intermediate CA if Redwood provides the CSR tooling. We prefer to avoid storing private keys outside our HSM.

I'll loop in our cloudops alias if needed, but the above covers the major constraints.

—Eric
Lead Cloud Ops, Telcoco

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Thanks all — summarizing next steps and owners so we can lock the diagram and runbook by Friday: 

1) PKI model: Telcoco will generate and sign an intermediate CA. Kimberly to validate CSR workflow and doc the rotation steps (owner: Kimberly; due: 2026-09-06).
2) Egress behavior: Telcoco keeps default egress in their NAT; Redwood will provide optional egress-relay toggle for canary. Jonas to add toggle to cutover checklist and mark logs we capture (owner: Jonas; due: 2026-09-07).
3) KV continuity: Marissa will add inter-proxy sync step and test plan for a 60s graceful window. She will schedule a short bench run with Telcoco (owner: Marissa; due: 2026-09-12).
4) Ports and allow-lists: Kimberly to produce the final port/ACL matrix for staging (owner: Kimberly; due: 2026-09-05).

I updated the Drive folder with the annotated diagram and a v1 cutover checklist link (https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/PrivateDeploy/CP-DP-Choreography-v1). Please add any further blockers there and mark items "blocked" / "ready" as you validate.

If there are no objections, I’ll freeze the diagram on 2026-09-08 and open the dry-run slot for 2026-09-15.

Jonas
